prerequisites: Apple silicon macOS host with a Metal device
reproduce.behavior: Builds the Verilator model and runs both backends during recording. Live, not playback.
reproduce.workspacePathConstraint: The tape uses absolute paths under /Volumes/Code/MuleinLabs and must be adjusted if the workspace moves.

capturedAtBasis: MP4 filesystem modification time at capture completion

captureMethod.mode: live execution of the comparison test

shellHelper.name: bench
shellHelper.body: swift test -c release --filter NativeBaselineComparisonTests 2>&1 | grep -E '^NATIVE_BASELINE' | fold -s -w 104
shellHelper.rationale: Keeps the typed command inside the terminal width. Its definition is echoed on screen before use.

toolchain.yosys: Yosys 0.68+post (git sha1 c12172fbae8af5e20f6fb52e3d4e92d56ed587b6, Release, AppleClang clang++ 21.0.0.21000101)

methodology.sharedArtifact: one emitted LUT6 Verilog file produced by TensorLUTEmitter
methodology.verilatorLineage: simulates that Verilog directly, compiled to native C++ at -O3
methodology.helutLineage: executes the $lut netlist yosys derives from the same file via abc -lut 6
methodology.equivalenceOfForms: established separately by SAT in TensorLUTMeltScalingTests
methodology.stimulus: identical assignments in identical order on both sides
methodology.verification: both sides fold outputs into one FNV-1a digest over (lane, wire, value); a mismatch invalidates the timings and fails the test
methodology.digestOrdering: by wire id rather than port-name string, because lexicographic name ordering differs between languages
methodology.excluded: build and compile time on both sides
methodology.helutWarmup: graph warmed before measurement; cold first-run JIT reported separately
methodology.verilatorTiming: self-timed inside the binary, so process startup is excluded

measurements.note: Values from this recorded run. Run-to-run variance of a few percent is expected and a separate run is preserved in HELUT/logs/helut-native-baseline-20260905T231427Z.log.
measurements.helutCostShape: essentially flat across a 65,536x range of work; dominated by fixed per-submission overhead

laterEvidenceAddendum.interpretation: This film remains a dated live observation of the earlier asymmetric graph-only comparison and its first tested historical win at B=65,536. It is not the current paired throughput verdict.
laterEvidenceAddendum.publicationBoundary: Use the later paired receipt for current performance wording. Do not replace or reinterpret the values visibly recorded in this historical MP4, and do not derive a digest-subtracted evaluator ratio.

claimBoundaries: This is a live run recorded on 2026-09-05, not playback of an archived log.
Verilator is single-threaded here and loops lanes sequentially. This is not a claim about Verilator's best achievable throughput; threading or batching it in C++ would move the crossover.
One combinational circuit on one machine. Nothing follows about sequential designs, larger circuits, or any other host.
Build and compile time are excluded on both sides, and HELUT is warmed before measurement, so this is steady-state cost rather than end-to-end time.
HELUT loses by roughly four orders of magnitude at a single instance. The result is a crossover, not a win.
The two backends execute different but provably equivalent forms of the same circuit: Verilator the LUT6 Verilog, HELUT the post-ABC $lut netlist.
Timings are local observations, not benchmark distributions.
Typed command echoes visibly wrap or overlap at some prompt boundaries; the projected table remains legible.
